title: Eastman Solus™ DBX Debuts in U.S. Food Service Through The Penny Ice Creamery
summary: Eastman announced the first U.S. commercial food service deployment of Solus™ DBX, its biobased coating for paper packaging, through The Penny Ice Creamery.
body_markdown:
Commercial deployment marks first U.S. food service use of Eastman’s biobased coating for paper packaging

**KINGSPORT, Tennessee**


Eastman today announced the first commercial deployment of Solus™ DBX-coated food service packaging to consumers in the United States through The Penny Ice Creamery, an independent ice cream operator based in Santa Cruz, California.


The Penny Ice Creamery is now serving customers ice cream in paper cups coated with Solus™ DBX across all locations. Solus™ DBX is Eastman’s biobased coating for paper food service packaging, with certain formulations containing up to 93% biobased content.


Created as an alternative to conventional low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and polylactic acid (PLA) liners, Solus™ DBX can support additional end-of-life pathways for certain coated paper articles — including industrial composting and paper recycling — depending on article design and local infrastructure.


"At Penny Ice Creamery, we believe that doing things the right way matters, from the ingredients in our ice cream to the cup it comes in,” said Zach Davis, co-owner of The Penny Ice Creamery. "Finding a cup that aligns with our sustainability values without compromising performance or the experience our customers expect is a priority for us. We're proud to be the first to bring this option to our guests."


Solus™ DBX is applied by converters to paper-based food service articles such as cups, bowls and to-go containers. It is designed to run on existing LDPE coating lines, helping converters adopt the technology without major capital investment. The coating delivers the moisture and oil-and-grease barrier performance food service operators require while enabling compostable and recyclable end-of-life pathways where appropriate infrastructure exists.


The deployment follows validation of Solus™ DBX under food service conditions. The coating has been assessed through third-party-accredited laboratory testing and validated in kitchen trials with leading national quick-service restaurant brands. Testing confirmed barrier performance, heat sealability and grease resistance under demanding food service use.


“Most people never think about the coating inside their cup,” said Mahendra Dorairaj, division president of coatings and inks at Eastman. “Solus™ DBX is designed to deliver the performance operators expect from today’s coatings while helping improve the end-of-life profile of coated paper packaging. The Penny Ice Creamery's willingness to lead on this is exactly the kind of partnership that makes progress real.”


Solus™ DBX, dependent on grade, holds industrial or home compostability certification from TÜV AUSTRIA and recyclability certification in the paper stream from the Western Michigan University Recycling Institute. Solus™ DBX formulations can also incorporate recycled content allocated via ISCC PLUS mass balance through Eastman’s innovative recycling technologies.


As food service operators evaluate packaging options amid evolving customer expectations and regulatory requirements, Eastman is working with converters and brand partners to expand availability of Solus™ DBX-coated articles. Additional converter partnerships are expected to launch in late 2026 and into 2027.


**About The Penny Ice Creamery**


As one of California’s smallest dairy manufacturing plants, The Penny Ice Creamery makes everything from scratch using local, seasonal and organic ingredients. Combining fresh local ingredients in small batches, they create artisanal ice cream in their shop, with all production done in full view of visitors. This transparency invites the community into the open kitchen and showcased production room, offering a unique behind-the-scenes look at what goes into crafting their delightful treats.


**About Eastman**


Founded in 1920, Eastman is a global specialty materials company that produces a broad range of products found in items people use every day. With the purpose of enhancing the quality of life in a material way, Eastman works with customers to deliver innovative products and solutions while maintaining a commitment to safety and sustainability. The company’s innovation-driven growth model takes advantage of world-class technology platforms, deep customer engagement, and differentiated application development to grow its leading positions in attractive end markets such as transportation, building and construction, and consumables. As a globally inclusive company, Eastman employs approximately 13,000 people around the world and serves customers in more than 100 countries. The company had 2025 revenue of approximately $8.8 billion and is headquartered in Kingsport, Tennessee, USA. For more information, visit[www.eastman.com](https://www.eastman.com/en) .
